gaps: Search count: 20 queries were logged here against a budget of 18 (the last two batches overran by two); no record depends on the two overrun queries except the Winning Wines fact, which earlier sweeps also hold.
Every record stands on a search engine summary of the Binwise list or the house dessert PDF, never a raw page read, so nothing is above medium. Check each against the printed list on shift.

Spain: no Spanish bottle on the Brennan's Binwise list surfaced in three searches (Rioja, Ribera del Duero, Vega Sicilia, López de Heredia, La Rioja Alta, CVNE, Muga). The only Spanish wines known are the Pazo das Bruxas Albariño by the glass (already in the pack) and the El Maestro Sierra PX on the dessert menu. Absence in search is not absence from the list.

Tuscany beyond Brunello: no Bolgheri, Sassicaia, Tignanello, Ornellaia or Chianti Classico tied to Brennan's. One summary said the list includes "several Brunello di Montalcino options" without names; the five magnums come from a second query.
Rest of Italy: no Alto Adige, Friuli, Etna, Veneto (Amarone, Soave), Campania or Sicily found. No Italian white of any kind found.

Piedmont: no 750 ml Barolo with a price surfaced; Giacomo Conterno, Bruno Giacosa and Bartolo Mascarello not found. Luigi Giordano Montestefano is named but has no vintage or price. Oddero Vigna Mondoca: which vintage is $475 and which $485 is unknown. Gaja Barbaresco 2020 format unstated.
Brunello: the summary printed "Fuglini"; the estate is almost certainly Fuligni, but the record keeps the printed form until the list is seen.

Germany: Keller "PIUS" is summarised as an Auslese at $245; Keller's Pius is usually a dry wine, so name and style need checking. Dönnhoff named without cuvée, vintage or price. No Egon Müller, J.J. Prüm, Saar or Rheingau bottle tied to Brennan's.
Austria: only the two Schloss Gobelsburg 2021 bottles; no Wachau (Hirtzberger, F.X. Pichler, Prager) found.

Portugal table wine, Greece, Hungary (Tokaji), Switzerland, Slovenia, Lebanon and the rest of Europe: nothing found. One dessert summary explicitly found no Tokaji or Banyuls on the dessert menu; the Banyuls in the pack is a tasting-menu pour.

Dessert menu PDF: undated, so it may predate the fall menus; the summaries give per glass only for the D'Oliveiras ($70) and Quinta Noval ($12) lines, the rest are presumed per glass. The full list may hold more lines (Muscat, ice wine, late harvest) that no snippet showed.

Madeira on Binwise: a summary spoke of Madeiras by the glass (Rare Wine Co. Historic Series, D'Oliveiras 1904 and 1908 Bual) and the Rare Wine Co. "New Orleans Special Reserve" Madeira, but did not tie any of it to Brennan's; nothing recorded. Worth asking whether the house pours the New Orleans Special Reserve.
No vintage Port bottle, no Sherry bottle beyond the PX glass, no Sauternes bottle (Yquem or other) found.
Fall menu changes after 26 September 2026 were not checked by this lens.
